codeReview.summary: Solid implementation of unicode display-width correctness across all four widgets. The truncate(), center(), and padOrTruncate() functions were correctly converted from rune-count-based to display-width-based using tui.RuneWidth(). Test coverage is thorough across all required unicode categories (CJK, combining marks, ZWJ emoji, RTL) and all four widgets (EntityList, DetailPane, StreamViewer, StatusBadge). All tests pass with -race. One non-blocking issue: the center() function contains ~15 lines of dead code (unused rune array construction) that should be cleaned up.

issues.description: Dead code in center(): lines 564-580 build a `result` rune array and write runes into it, but the final return at line 584-586 uses string concatenation (`leftPad + s + rightPad`) instead. The entire `result` slice, the loop writing into it, and the surrounding comments are unused. This is a leftover from the iterative fix — the worker abandoned the rune-array approach in favor of string concatenation but forgot to remove the dead code. The function is correct (returns the right output), but the dead code is confusing and wastes allocation.

TestUnicodePadOrTruncateWidth only has one test case (CJK string with width 8). It could benefit from more edge cases: exact-width CJK string, ASCII-only string, combining marks. This is minor since padOrTruncate() now delegates to truncate() which has better coverage.

TestUnicodeCenterWidth only has one test case (center("研究", 10)). Could benefit from edge cases: odd-width padding, string exactly filling width, string exceeding width. The underlying center() function works correctly for these cases, but test coverage is thin for the centering logic specifically.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The tui.RuneWidth() function from grindlemire/go-tui is the canonical way to compute terminal display width for unicode characters. This is important for any widget that truncates or pads strings. The library handles CJK (width=2), combining marks (width=0), ZWJ sequences (width=2 for emoji), and RTL correctly. This knowledge should be in .factory/library/ for future widget work.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: entity_list.go:530 uses tui.RuneWidth(r), small_primitives.go references runeWidth() helper which also uses tui.RuneWidth(). Both truncate() and padOrTruncate() now rely on display width rather than rune count.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The pattern of 'render width' vs 'rune count' was a bug class across the TUI component library. The original truncate(), center(), and padOrTruncate() all used len([]rune(s)) which is wrong for CJK/emoji. The fix pattern (iterate string with range, accumulate tui.RuneWidth per rune) should be documented as the standard approach for any new string-width-aware code.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: entity_list.go truncate() lines 514-545, center() lines 555-586, small_primitives.go padOrTruncate() lines 296-310 all follow the same pattern now.

summary: PASS. The feature correctly implements unicode display-width awareness across all four required widgets with 34+ test cases covering all four unicode categories (CJK ideographs, combining diacritical marks, ZWJ emoji, RTL strings). The three utility functions (truncate, center, padOrTruncate) were fixed from rune-count to display-width semantics. The CJK snapshot with 研究員/コーダー/計画者 role labels exists and is verified. All tests pass with -race. One non-blocking dead-code issue in center() (unused rune array construction) should be cleaned up in a follow-up. Test coverage for center() and padOrTruncateWidth utility tests is thin but acceptable since the widget-level tests exercise these functions indirectly.
